claim: Ablation of the core clock within the endocrine pancreas of adult animals impairs the transcription and splicing of genes involved in hormone exocytosis.
source: Ablation of the core clock within the endocrine pancreas of adult animals impairs the transcription and splicing of genes involved in hormone exocytosis and causes hypoinsulinemic diabetes.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work and is consistent with the experimental findings presented in the manuscript.

claim: Ablation of the core clock within the endocrine pancreas of adult animals causes hypoinsulinemic diabetes.
source: Ablation of the core clock within the endocrine pancreas of adult animals impairs the transcription and splicing of genes involved in hormone exocytosis and causes hypoinsulinemic diabetes.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work and is consistent with the experimental findings presented in the manuscript.

claim: A genetically sensitized small-molecule screen was developed to identify druggable proteins and mechanistic pathways involved in circadian β-cell failure.
source: Here, we developed a genetically sensitized small-molecule screen to identify druggable proteins and mechanistic pathways involved in circadian β-cell failure.
evidence: The manuscript describes the development and execution of this screening approach.

claim: β-cells expressing a nanoluciferase reporter within the proinsulin polypeptide were generated to screen 2640 pharmacologically active compounds.
source: Our approach was to generate β-cells expressing a nanoluciferase reporter within the proinsulin polypeptide to screen 2640 pharmacologically active compounds and identify insulinotropic molecules that bypass the secretory defect in CRISPR-Cas9-targeted clock mutant β-cells.
evidence: The manuscript describes the generation of these cells and their use in screening.

claim: The screen identified insulinotropic molecules that bypass the secretory defect in CRISPR-Cas9-targeted clock mutant β-cells.
source: Our approach was to generate β-cells expressing a nanoluciferase reporter within the proinsulin polypeptide to screen 2640 pharmacologically active compounds and identify insulinotropic molecules that bypass the secretory defect in CRISPR-Cas9-targeted clock mutant β-cells.
evidence: The manuscript presents data showing compounds that enhance insulin secretion in clock mutant cells.

claim: Hit compounds were validated in primary mouse islets.
source: We validated hit compounds in primary mouse islets and identified known modulators of ligand-gated ion channels and G-protein-coupled receptors, including the antihelmintic ivermectin.
evidence: The manuscript presents ELISA data from primary mouse islets treated with hit compounds.

claim: Known modulators of ligand-gated ion channels and G-protein-coupled receptors were identified, including the antihelmintic ivermectin.
source: We validated hit compounds in primary mouse islets and identified known modulators of ligand-gated ion channels and G-protein-coupled receptors, including the antihelmintic ivermectin.
evidence: The manuscript identifies ivermectin and other compounds with known mechanisms of action.

claim: Single-cell electrophysiology in circadian mutant mouse islets revealed ivermectin as a glucose-dependent secretagogue.
source: Single-cell electrophysiology in circadian mutant mouse and human cadaveric islets revealed ivermectin as a glucose-dependent secretagogue.
evidence: The manuscript presents capacitance measurements showing ivermectin enhances exocytosis in a glucose-dependent manner.

claim: Single-cell electrophysiology in human cadaveric islets revealed ivermectin as a glucose-dependent secretagogue.
source: Single-cell electrophysiology in circadian mutant mouse and human cadaveric islets revealed ivermectin as a glucose-dependent secretagogue.
evidence: The manuscript presents capacitance measurements in human islets showing ivermectin enhances exocytosis.

claim: The P2Y1 receptor was established as a clock-controlled mediator of the insulinotropic activity of ivermectin through genetic, genomic, and pharmacological analyses.
source: Genetic, genomic, and pharmacological analyses established the P2Y1 receptor as a clock-controlled mediator of the insulinotropic activity of ivermectin.
evidence: The manuscript presents multiple lines of evidence including CRISPR knockout, RNA-seq, ChIP-seq, and pharmacological inhibition.

claim: The P2Y1 purinergic receptor is identified as a diabetes target based upon a genetically sensitized phenotypic screen.
source: These findings identify the P2Y1 purinergic receptor as a diabetes target based upon a genetically sensitized phenotypic screen.
evidence: The manuscript presents data showing P2Y1 mediates insulin secretion and is controlled by the circadian clock.

claim: Shift work and sleep disturbance are environmental risk factors for diabetes.
source: Recent epidemiological evidence has shown that shift work and sleep disturbance are environmental risk factors for diabetes (Perelis et al., 2016), while experimental genetic studies have shown that clock gene disruption within the endocrine pancreas causes hypoinsulinemic diabetes (Marcheva et al., 2010; Sadacca et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to epidemiological studies.

claim: Clock gene disruption within the endocrine pancreas causes hypoinsulinemic diabetes.
source: Recent epidemiological evidence has shown that shift work and sleep disturbance are environmental risk factors for diabetes (Perelis et al., 2016), while experimental genetic studies have shown that clock gene disruption within the endocrine pancreas causes hypoinsulinemic diabetes (Marcheva et al., 2010; Sadacca et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to experimental genetic studies.

claim: The circadian clock is composed of an autoregulatory transcriptional loop in which CLOCK/BMAL1 activate the repressors PER1/2/3 and CRY1/2, which feedback to inhibit CLOCK/BMAL1 in a cycle that repeats itself every 24 hr.
source: At the molecular level, the circadian clock is composed of an autoregulatory transcriptional loop in which CLOCK/BMAL1 activate the repressors PER1/2/3 and CRY1/2, which feedback to inhibit CLOCK/BMAL1 in a cycle that repeats itself every 24 hr.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the molecular circadian clock mechanism.

claim: An additional stabilizing loop involving ROR/REV-ERB regulates BMAL1 expression.
source: An additional stabilizing loop involving ROR/REV-ERB regulates BMAL1 expression (Kim and Lazar, 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Casein kinase 1 inhibitors lengthen the circadian period through stabilizing PER proteins.
source: Recent chemical screens have identified new factors that modulate the core clock, including casein kinase 1 inhibitors that lengthen the circadian period through stabilizing PER proteins (Hirota et al., 2010; Chen et al., 2012), and a separate series of cryptochrome stabilizer compounds have been discovered that control glucose homeostasis in vivo (Hirota et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior chemical screens.

claim: Cryptochrome stabilizer compounds control glucose homeostasis in vivo.
source: Recent chemical screens have identified new factors that modulate the core clock, including casein kinase 1 inhibitors that lengthen the circadian period through stabilizing PER proteins (Hirota et al., 2010; Chen et al., 2012), and a separate series of cryptochrome stabilizer compounds have been discovered that control glucose homeostasis in vivo (Hirota et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Modulators of clock transcription factors may control whole animal metabolism.
source: Modulators of clock transcription factors may also control whole animal metabolism (He et al., 2016), though such compounds lack specificity (Dierickx et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Clock transcription factor modulators lack specificity.
source: Modulators of clock transcription factors may also control whole animal metabolism (He et al., 2016), though such compounds lack specificity (Dierickx et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Clonal Bmal1-/- Beta-TC-6 β-cell lines recapitulate the secretory defects observed in primary clock-deficient islets.
source: We previously showed that clonal Bmal1-/- Beta-TC-6 β-cell lines recapitulate the secretory defects observed in primary clock-deficient islets (Marcheva et al., 2010; Perelis et al., 2015; Marcheva et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work by the authors.

claim: There is a direct correspondence between insulin-NanoLuc bioluminescence and levels of peptide secretion under increasing physiological concentrations of glucose (2–20 mM; R2 = 0.8937).
source: We validated the direct correspondence between insulin-NanoLuc bioluminescence and levels of peptide secretion under increasing physiological concentrations of glucose (2–20 mM; R2 = 0.8937; Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing correlation between bioluminescence and ELISA measurements.

claim: Bmal1-/- β-cell lines expressing insulin-NanoLuc show impaired insulin secretion compared to WT in response to stimulatory concentrations of glucose (20 mM), potassium chloride, forskolin, and IBMX.
source: We further confirmed impaired insulin secretion by reduced bioluminescence in Bmal1-/- compared to WT β-cell lines expressing insulin-NanoLuc in response to stimulatory concentrations of glucose (20 mM), potassium chloride, forskolin, and the phosphodiesterase inhibitor 3-isobutyl-1-methylxanthine (IBMX) (Figure 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by bioluminescence data comparing WT and Bmal1-/- cells.

claim: PMA was validated as a positive control for the screen.
source: We also validated the use of the DAG mimetic phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate (PMA) as a positive control for the screen (Figure 1D–F; Perelis et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data and citation to prior work.

claim: A feasibility test with a Z'-factor score of 0.69 indicated a significant separation between the distribution of bioluminescent signal from the positive and negative controls.
source: A feasibility test with a Z'-factor score of 0.69 indicated a significant separation between the distribution of bioluminescent signal from the positive (10 μM PMA + 20 mM glucose) and negative (20 mM glucose) controls, suggesting that the assay provides a suitable platform for a high-throughput screen (Figure 1F; Zhang et al., 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of the assay performance.

claim: The assay provides a suitable platform for a high-throughput screen.
source: A feasibility test with a Z'-factor score of 0.69 indicated a significant separation between the distribution of bioluminescent signal from the positive (10 μM PMA + 20 mM glucose) and negative (20 mM glucose) controls, suggesting that the assay provides a suitable platform for a high-throughput screen (Figure 1F; Zhang et al., 1999).
evidence: This claim is inferred from the Z'-factor score meeting accepted criteria for screening assays.

claim: 19 hit compounds were initially identified that both significantly enhanced insulin secretion and elicited a response of greater than 3 standard deviations from the mean (Z-score > 3) with more than a 1.25-fold increase.
source: We initially identified 19 hit compounds that both significantly enhanced insulin secretion and elicited a response of greater than 3 standard deviations from the mean (Z-score > 3) with more than a 1.25-fold increase, exceeding the upper 99% confidence interval of the negative control (Figure 2A, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by the screening data and statistical analysis.

claim: Seven hit compounds were excluded from further analysis because of reported toxic effects or lack of availability of the compound.
source: Of these, seven were excluded from further analysis because of reported toxic effects or lack of availability of the compound (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a methodological decision based on literature and practical considerations.

claim: The remaining 12 hit compounds mediate activity of ligand-gated cell surface receptors and ion channels that stimulate second messenger signaling cascades.
source: The remaining 12 hit compounds mediate activity of ligand-gated cell surface receptors and ion channels that stimulate second messenger signaling cascades (Figure 2B and C; Gaulton et al., 2010; Carrano et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is based on known mechanisms of action of the compounds, supported by citations.

claim: Four hit compounds target ion channels (tacrine hydrochloride, suloctidil, dyclonine hydrochloride, and IVM).
source: Of these, four target ion channels (tacrine hydrochloride, suloctidil, dyclonine hydrochloride, and IVM) (Figure 2B and C; Karlsson and Ahrén, 1992; Chatelain et al., 1984; Khanna et al., 2011; Chen and Kubo, 2018; Freeman et al., 1988; de Gaetano et al., 1976; Kornhuber et al., 2008; Sahdeo et al., 2014; Roghani et al., 1999; Ikeda, 2003).
evidence: This claim is based on known mechanisms of action of the compounds, supported by citations.

claim: Five hit compounds target seven-transmembrane G-protein coupled receptors (GPCRs) that signal through phospholipase C (PLC) and diacylglycerol (DAG) to activate insulin secretion and β-cell gene transcription.
source: Five target seven-transmembrane G-protein coupled receptors (GPCRs) that signal through phospholipase C (PLC) and diacylglycerol (DAG) to activate insulin secretion and β-cell gene transcription (benzalkonium chloride, carbachol, isoetharine mesylate, pipamperone, and IVM) (Figure 2B and C; Chen and Kubo, 2018; Higashijima et al., 1990; Rinne et al., 2015; Bierman, 1983; Van Craenenbroeck et al., 2006; Nagata et al., 2019; Ratajewski et al., 2015; Ohtani et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is based on known mechanisms of action of the compounds, supported by citations.

claim: Carbachol, a muscarinic Gq-coupled receptor agonist, and the DAG mimetic PMA rescue insulin secretion in Bmal1-/- islets.
source: Similar to the hit compounds of our screen, our previous results showed that carbachol, a muscarinic Gq-coupled receptor agonist, and the DAG mimetic PMA rescue insulin secretion in Bmal1-/- islets (Perelis et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work by the authors.

claim: Four hit compounds act as acetylcholinesterase inhibitors, promoting enhanced glucose-dependent insulin secretion in response to acetylcholine through the muscarinic GPCRs and the ionotropic nicotinic acetylcholine receptors.
source: Four additional hit compounds act as acetylcholinesterase inhibitors, promoting enhanced glucose-dependent insulin secretion in response to acetylcholine through the muscarinic GPCRs, as well as the ionotropic nicotinic acetylcholine receptors (tyrothricin, tomatine, carbachol, and tacrine hydrochloride) (Figure 2B and C; Changeux et al., 1969; Milner et al., 2011; Rosenberry et al., 2008; Marco and Carreiras, 2003; Lang and Staiger, 2016; Shih et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is based on known mechanisms of action of the compounds, supported by citations.

claim: Alexidine hydrochloride promotes insulin secretion by inhibition of the mitochondrial protein tyrosine phosphatase PTPM1.
source: One compound has been shown to promote insulin secretion by inhibition of the mitochondrial protein tyrosine phosphatase PTPM1 (alexidine hydrochloride) (Figure 2B and C; Doughty-Shenton et al., 2010; Nath et al., 2015), and another likely affects β-cell function by signaling through the mineralocorticoid receptor (deoxycorticosterone) (Figure 2B and C; Lu et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is based on known mechanisms of action, supported by citations.

claim: Deoxycorticosterone likely affects β-cell function by signaling through the mineralocorticoid receptor.
source: One compound has been shown to promote insulin secretion by inhibition of the mitochondrial protein tyrosine phosphatase PTPM1 (alexidine hydrochloride) (Figure 2B and C; Doughty-Shenton et al., 2010; Nath et al., 2015), and another likely affects β-cell function by signaling through the mineralocorticoid receptor (deoxycorticosterone) (Figure 2B and C; Lu et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is based on known mechanisms of action, supported by citations.

claim: IVM signals in micromolar concentrations through several ionotropic receptors, including purinergic, GABAergic, and glycine receptors, as well as through the farnesoid X nuclear receptor.
source: Finally, in addition to ion channels and GPCRs, the macrolide IVM has also been shown to signal in micromolar concentrations though several ionotropic receptors, including purinergic, GABAergic, and glycine receptors, as well as through the farnesoid X nuclear receptor (Chen and Kubo, 2018; Dawson et al., 2000; Soltani et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is based on known mechanisms of action of IVM, supported by citations.

claim: 10 of the 12 hit compounds were not considered for further analysis because of either the high dose required to achieve insulin secretion or because they augmented insulin release in low basal glucose (2 mM) in intact WT mouse primary islets.
source: 10 of these 12 hit compounds were not considered for further analysis because of either the high dose required to achieve insulin secretion (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B) or because they augmented insulin release in low basal glucose (2 mM) in intact WT mouse primary islets (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is a methodological decision based on experimental validation data.

claim: Tacrine hydrochloride induces hepatotoxicity after prolonged use.
source: One of the remaining compounds induces hepatotoxicity after prolonged use (tacrine hydrochloride) (Galisteo et al., 2000).
evidence: This claim is based on known toxicity of the compound, supported by citation.

claim: IVM shows dose-dependent enhancement of GSIS in insulin-NanoLuc-expressing Beta-TC-6 cells.
source: We therefore focused our attention on IVM due to its dose-dependent enhancement of GSIS in insulin-NanoLuc-expressing Beta-TC-6 cells, as well as its robust rescue of insulin secretion in Bmal1-/- islets (Figure 2D and E).
evidence: This claim is supported by dose-response curve data.

claim: IVM robustly rescues insulin secretion in Bmal1-/- islets.
source: We therefore focused our attention on IVM due to its dose-dependent enhancement of GSIS in insulin-NanoLuc-expressing Beta-TC-6 cells, as well as its robust rescue of insulin secretion in Bmal1-/- islets (Figure 2D and E).
evidence: This claim is supported by ELISA data from Bmal1-/- islets.

claim: IVM enhanced insulin secretion in a glucose-dependent manner following both 1 hr IVM exposure and 24 hr pretreatment with IVM in β-cell lines and WT mouse islets.
source: Consistent with our initial bioluminescence assay, we observed that IVM enhanced insulin secretion in a glucose-dependent manner following both 1 hr IVM exposure and 24 hr pretreatment with IVM in β-cell lines and WT mouse islets, suggesting that both acute and longer-term exposure to IVM enhance β-cell function (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data comparing acute and overnight IVM treatment.

claim: Both acute and longer-term exposure to IVM enhance β-cell function.
source: Consistent with our initial bioluminescence assay, we observed that IVM enhanced insulin secretion in a glucose-dependent manner following both 1 hr IVM exposure and 24 hr pretreatment with IVM in β-cell lines and WT mouse islets, suggesting that both acute and longer-term exposure to IVM enhance β-cell function (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that both acute and overnight treatments enhance insulin secretion.

claim: IVM causes an immediate and robust glucose-stimulated intracellular calcium response within 2 min of IVM stimulation (p<0.05).
source: We observed an immediate and robust glucose-stimulated intracellular calcium response within 2 min of IVM stimulation (p<0.05) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by calcium imaging data.

claim: The IVM effect on calcium influx was only observed in the presence of high glucose.
source: Importantly, this effect was only observed in the presence of high glucose, consistent with results of our initial NanoLuc 384-well plate screening and subsequent ELISA-based analyses of GSIS.
evidence: This claim is supported by calcium imaging data showing glucose-dependence.

claim: The Ca2+ channel inhibitor isradipine completely suppressed Ca2+ influx and insulin secretion.
source: In contrast, the Ca2+ channel inhibitor isradipine completely suppressed Ca2+ influx and insulin secretion (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and D; Berjukow et al., 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data using the calcium channel inhibitor.

claim: IVM significantly increased insulin release during the initial burst of secretion within the first 12 min post-stimulation (p<0.05).
source: IVM significantly increased insulin release during the initial burst of secretion within the first 12 min post-stimulation (p<0.05) and continued to enhance insulin secretion during the remainder of the stimulation period (12–30 min), consistent with continuous release of reserve insulin granules (Rorsman and Renström, 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by perifusion data.

claim: IVM continued to enhance insulin secretion during the remainder of the stimulation period (12–30 min), consistent with continuous release of reserve insulin granules.
source: IVM significantly increased insulin release during the initial burst of secretion within the first 12 min post-stimulation (p<0.05) and continued to enhance insulin secretion during the remainder of the stimulation period (12–30 min), consistent with continuous release of reserve insulin granules (Rorsman and Renström, 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by perifusion data and citation to prior work on insulin granule release kinetics.

claim: IVM administration to mouse islets isolated from pancreas-specific Bmal1-/- mice revealed a 3.3-fold elevation of GSIS following exposure to the drug in the Bmal1 mutant islets.
source: To test this idea, we administered IVM to mouse islets isolated from pancreas-specific Bmal1-/- mice, revealing a 3.3-fold elevation of GSIS following exposure to the drug in the Bmal1 mutant islets (Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by ELISA data from Bmal1-/- islets.

claim: Perifusion experiments in islets from Bmal1 mutant mice revealed that IVM significantly increased insulin release during both the initial burst of secretion (first 12 min post-stimulation) and during the sustained release (12–30 min) in both WT and Bmal1 mutant islets.
source: Furthermore, perifusion experiments in islets from Bmal1 mutant mice revealed that IVM significantly increased insulin release during both the initial burst of secretion (first 12 min post-stimulation) and during the sustained release (12–30 min) in both WT and Bmal1 mutant islets (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by perifusion data from WT and Bmal1 mutant islets.

claim: A 2.9-fold increase in GSIS was observed following administration of IVM to islets isolated from Cry1-/-;Cry2-/- mice.
source: Additionally, we observed a similar 2.9-fold increase in GSIS following administration of IVM to islets isolated from an independent mouse model of circadian disruption (Cry1-/-;Cry2-/- mice) (Figure 3D), suggesting that IVM ameliorates secretory defects caused by disruption of the circadian clock network.
evidence: This claim is supported by ELISA data from Cry double mutant islets.

claim: IVM ameliorates secretory defects caused by disruption of the circadian clock network.
source: Additionally, we observed a similar 2.9-fold increase in GSIS following administration of IVM to islets isolated from an independent mouse model of circadian disruption (Cry1-/-;Cry2-/- mice) (Figure 3D), suggesting that IVM ameliorates secretory defects caused by disruption of the circadian clock network.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that IVM rescues insulin secretion in two different circadian mutant models.

claim: Daily intraperitoneal IVM (1.3 mg/kg body weight) administered to Akita mice over a 14-day period significantly improved glucose tolerance.
source: Daily intraperitoneal IVM (1.3 mg/kg body weight) was administered to Akita mice over a 14-day period (Jin et al., 2013), terminating in assessment of glucose tolerance and ex vivo GSIS. Treatment with IVM significantly improved glucose tolerance and augmented glucose-stimulated insulin release from islets isolated from these mice (Figure 3—figure supplement 1F and G).
evidence: This claim is supported by glucose tolerance test data from Akita mice.

claim: Daily intraperitoneal IVM (1.3 mg/kg body weight) administered to Akita mice over a 14-day period augmented glucose-stimulated insulin release from islets isolated from these mice.
source: Daily intraperitoneal IVM (1.3 mg/kg body weight) was administered to Akita mice over a 14-day period (Jin et al., 2013), terminating in assessment of glucose tolerance and ex vivo GSIS. Treatment with IVM significantly improved glucose tolerance and augmented glucose-stimulated insulin release from islets isolated from these mice (Figure 3—figure supplement 1F and G).
evidence: This claim is supported by ELISA data from Akita mouse islets.

claim: Bmal1 mutant cells displayed reduced rates of exocytosis following direct depolarization (as indicated by reduced capacitance).
source: While Bmal1 mutant cells displayed reduced rates of exocytosis following direct depolarization (as indicated by reduced capacitance), 10 µM IVM treatment rescued the defect in Bmal1 mutant cells, increasing cumulative capacitance from 11.0 to 20.7 fF/pF after 10 consecutive depolarization steps (Figure 3E).
evidence: This claim is supported by patch-clamp electrophysiology data.

claim: 10 µM IVM treatment rescued the exocytosis defect in Bmal1 mutant cells, increasing cumulative capacitance from 11.0 to 20.7 fF/pF after 10 consecutive depolarization steps.
source: While Bmal1 mutant cells displayed reduced rates of exocytosis following direct depolarization (as indicated by reduced capacitance), 10 µM IVM treatment rescued the defect in Bmal1 mutant cells, increasing cumulative capacitance from 11.0 to 20.7 fF/pF after 10 consecutive depolarization steps (Figure 3E).
evidence: This claim is supported by patch-clamp electrophysiology data.

claim: IVM treatment enhanced cumulative capacitance in human β-cells from 17.9 to 39.7 fF/pF.
source: IVM treatment also enhanced cumulative capacitance in human β-cells from 17.9 to 39.7 fF/pF (Figure 3F).
evidence: This claim is supported by patch-clamp electrophysiology data from human islets.

claim: IVM augments β-cell early calcium influx in a glucose-dependent manner to promote increased vesicle fusion and release.
source: Together, these data show that IVM augments β-cell early calcium influx in a glucose-dependent manner to promote increased vesicle fusion and release.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the calcium imaging and capacitance data presented.

claim: P2ry1 was identified as the most highly expressed putative IVM target in wild-type β-cells.
source: We first identified the purinergic receptor P2Y1 (P2ry1) as the most highly expressed putative IVM target in wild-type β-cells (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq expression data.

claim: P2ry1 was one of the most highly downregulated targets in Bmal1-/- cells, with mRNA expression levels reduced by ~3.1-fold (adjusted p=10–55).
source: We then observed that P2ry1 was one of the most highly downregulated targets in Bmal1-/- cells, with mRNA expression levels reduced by ~3.1-fold (adjusted p=10–55; Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A; GSE146916).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq differential expression analysis.

claim: Decreased levels and loss in rhythmicity of P2ry1 were found in synchronized Bmal1-/- pseudoislets.
source: We found decreased levels and loss in rhythmicity of P2ry1 in synchronized Bmal1-/- pseudoislets (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by qPCR time-course data.

claim: BMAL1 chromatin immunoprecipitation-sequencing in Beta-TC-6 cells revealed enrichment of BMAL1 chromatin binding within enhancer regions 266–41 kb upstream of the P2ry1 gene transcription start site.
source: BMAL1 chromatin immunoprecipitation-sequencing in Beta-TC-6 cells further revealed enrichment of BMAL1 chromatin binding within enhancer regions 266–41 kb upstream of the P2ry1 gene transcription start site (GSE69889; Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-seq data.

claim: Analysis of RNA-sequencing data from human islets indicates that P2RY1 expression is enriched within β-cells among hormone-secreting cell types, with little to no detectable expression in the glucagon-secreting α cells.
source: Finally, analysis of RNA-sequencing data from human islets (SRA accession ERP017126) indicates that P2RY1 expression is enriched within β-cells among hormone-secreting cell types, with little to no detectable expression in the glucagon-secreting α cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C; Segerstolpe et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by analysis of published single-cell RNA-seq data from human islets.

claim: The data reveal direct rhythmic control of the P2ry1 gene by the β-cell circadian clock.
source: Together, these data reveal direct rhythmic control of the P2ry1 gene by the β-cell circadian clock.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the ChIP-seq, RNA-seq, and rhythmic expression data.

claim: Pharmacological inhibition of P2Y1 using MRS2179 in the presence of both high glucose and 10 μM IVM resulted in a 52% reduction in insulin secretion by bioluminescence.
source: Pharmacological inhibition of P2Y1 using a subtype-specific inhibitor, the nucleotide analog MRS2179, in the presence of both high glucose and 10 μM IVM resulted in a 52% reduction in insulin secretion by bioluminescence and a reduction in calcium influx to levels similar to those observed during high glucose alone, as assessed by Fura2-AM ratiometric determination of intracellular calcium (Figure 4B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by bioluminescence data with pharmacological inhibitor.

claim: Pharmacological inhibition of P2Y1 using MRS2179 in the presence of both high glucose and 10 μM IVM resulted in a reduction in calcium influx to levels similar to those observed during high glucose alone.
source: Pharmacological inhibition of P2Y1 using a subtype-specific inhibitor, the nucleotide analog MRS2179, in the presence of both high glucose and 10 μM IVM resulted in a 52% reduction in insulin secretion by bioluminescence and a reduction in calcium influx to levels similar to those observed during high glucose alone, as assessed by Fura2-AM ratiometric determination of intracellular calcium (Figure 4B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by calcium imaging data with pharmacological inhibitor.

claim: IVM enhanced GSIS in WT β-cells 1.6-fold.
source: While IVM enhanced GSIS in WT and Bmal1-/-β-cells 1.6- and 1.8-fold, respectively, IVM did not significantly enhance GSIS in cells lacking the P2Y1 receptor (Figure 4D).
evidence: This claim is supported by ELISA data from WT cells.

claim: IVM enhanced GSIS in Bmal1-/- β-cells 1.8-fold.
source: While IVM enhanced GSIS in WT and Bmal1-/-β-cells 1.6- and 1.8-fold, respectively, IVM did not significantly enhance GSIS in cells lacking the P2Y1 receptor (Figure 4D).
evidence: This claim is supported by ELISA data from Bmal1-/- cells.

claim: IVM did not significantly enhance GSIS in cells lacking the P2Y1 receptor.
source: While IVM enhanced GSIS in WT and Bmal1-/-β-cells 1.6- and 1.8-fold, respectively, IVM did not significantly enhance GSIS in cells lacking the P2Y1 receptor (Figure 4D).
evidence: This claim is supported by ELISA data from P2ry1 knockout cells.

claim: These results demonstrate a requirement for P2Y1 in IVM-induced GSIS.
source: Similar to the pharmacological findings with the P2Y1 antagonist MRS2179, these results demonstrate a requirement for P2Y1 in IVM-induced GSIS.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the genetic knockout and pharmacological inhibition data.

claim: Principal component analysis revealed distinct patterns in mRNA expression between IVM- and control-treated WT cells along PC2.
source: This revealed distinct patterns in mRNA expression between IVM- and control-treated WT cells along PC2, while there was no separation between IVM- and control-treated P2ry1-/- β-cells, suggesting that P2Y1 is required for IVM-mediated transcriptional changes in β-cells (Figure 4E).
evidence: This claim is supported by PCA analysis of RNA-seq data.

claim: There was no separation between IVM- and control-treated P2ry1-/- β-cells in principal component analysis.
source: This revealed distinct patterns in mRNA expression between IVM- and control-treated WT cells along PC2, while there was no separation between IVM- and control-treated P2ry1-/- β-cells, suggesting that P2Y1 is required for IVM-mediated transcriptional changes in β-cells (Figure 4E).
evidence: This claim is supported by PCA analysis of RNA-seq data.

claim: P2Y1 is required for IVM-mediated transcriptional changes in β-cells.
source: This revealed distinct patterns in mRNA expression between IVM- and control-treated WT cells along PC2, while there was no separation between IVM- and control-treated P2ry1-/- β-cells, suggesting that P2Y1 is required for IVM-mediated transcriptional changes in β-cells (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is inferred from the PCA analysis showing transcriptional changes only in WT cells.

claim: In WT cells, IVM induced differential expression of 65 transcripts (1.5-fold change, adjusted p-value<0.05).
source: In WT cells, IVM induced differential expression of 65 transcripts (1.5-fold change, adjusted p-value<0.05), including upregulation of the immediate early gene Fos (Murphy et al., 1991) and downregulation of Aldolase B, whose expression has been linked to reduced insulin secretion in human islets (Gerst et al., 2018; Figure 4F, Figure 4—figure supplement 2B, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq differential expression analysis.

claim: IVM induced upregulation of the immediate early gene Fos in WT cells.
source: In WT cells, IVM induced differential expression of 65 transcripts (1.5-fold change, adjusted p-value<0.05), including upregulation of the immediate early gene Fos (Murphy et al., 1991) and downregulation of Aldolase B, whose expression has been linked to reduced insulin secretion in human islets (Gerst et al., 2018; Figure 4F, Figure 4—figure supplement 2B, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data and citation to prior work on Fos.

claim: IVM induced downregulation of Aldolase B in WT cells, whose expression has been linked to reduced insulin secretion in human islets.
source: In WT cells, IVM induced differential expression of 65 transcripts (1.5-fold change, adjusted p-value<0.05), including upregulation of the immediate early gene Fos (Murphy et al., 1991) and downregulation of Aldolase B, whose expression has been linked to reduced insulin secretion in human islets (Gerst et al., 2018; Figure 4F, Figure 4—figure supplement 2B, Supplementary file 2).

claim: None of the 65 transcripts differentially expressed by IVM in WT cells were significantly altered by IVM in the P2ry1-/- β-cells (all adjusted p-value>0.05).
source: Strikingly, none of these transcripts were significantly altered by IVM in the P2ry1-/- β-cells (all adjusted p-value>0.05) (Figure 4F, Figure 4—figure supplement 2B, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq differential expression analysis in P2ry1 knockout cells.

claim: The circadian clock program controls P2Y1 expression to modulate GSIS.
source: Taken together, these data suggest that the circadian clock program controls P2Y1 expression to modulate GSIS and highlight the utility of a genetic-sensitized drug screen for identification of therapeutic targets in circadian dysregulation and diabetes.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the ChIP-seq, RNA-seq, and functional data.

claim: A genetic-sensitized drug screen has utility for identification of therapeutic targets in circadian dysregulation and diabetes.
source: Taken together, these data suggest that the circadian clock program controls P2Y1 expression to modulate GSIS and highlight the utility of a genetic-sensitized drug screen for identification of therapeutic targets in circadian dysregulation and diabetes.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the methodological approach based on the successful identification of P2Y1.

claim: P2Y receptors have been previously implicated in calcium and insulin secretory dynamics in β-cells.
source: While P2Y receptors have been previously implicated in calcium and insulin secretory dynamics in β-cells, modulation has been primarily demonstrated using agonists that mimic ATP/ADP derivatives that have deleterious effects on thrombosis (Léon et al., 2005; Khan et al., 2014; Balasubramanian et al., 2010; Gąsecka et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is based on prior literature, supported by citations.

claim: Modulation of P2Y receptors has been primarily demonstrated using agonists that mimic ATP/ADP derivatives that have deleterious effects on thrombosis.
source: While P2Y receptors have been previously implicated in calcium and insulin secretory dynamics in β-cells, modulation has been primarily demonstrated using agonists that mimic ATP/ADP derivatives that have deleterious effects on thrombosis (Léon et al., 2005; Khan et al., 2014; Balasubramanian et al., 2010; Gąsecka et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is based on prior literature, supported by citations.

source: Little is known about P2Y1 targeting in disease states, such as circadian disruption and/or type 2 diabetes, or whether P2Y1 is controlled at a transcriptional level.

evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Evidence that P2Y1 is expressed under control of the circadian clock derives from analyses at the level of both chromatin binding by the core clock factor BMAL1 and genome-wide differential RNA expression analysis in circadian mutants.
source: Our evidence that P2Y1 is expressed under control of the circadian clock derives from analyses at the level of both chromatin binding by the core clock factor BMAL1 and genome-wide differential RNA expression analysis in circadian mutants.
evidence: This is a summary of the evidence presented in the manuscript.

claim: P2X and P2Y receptors are required for Ca2+ signaling in the suprachiasmatic nucleus.
source: Intriguingly, P2X and P2Y receptors are required for Ca2+ signaling in the suprachiasmatic nucleus (Lommen et al., 2017; Svobodova et al., 2018), yet their role in circadian regulation of peripheral tissues has not been well studied.
evidence: This claim is based on prior literature, supported by citations.

claim: The role of P2X and P2Y receptors in circadian regulation of peripheral tissues has not been well studied.
source: Intriguingly, P2X and P2Y receptors are required for Ca2+ signaling in the suprachiasmatic nucleus (Lommen et al., 2017; Svobodova et al., 2018), yet their role in circadian regulation of peripheral tissues has not been well studied.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field.

claim: IVM action requires the presence of P2Y1 receptors in β-cells since functional ablation of the P2Y1 receptor attenuates the effect of IVM on insulin secretion in both wild-type and circadian mutant β-cells.
source: Our data suggests that IVM action requires the presence of P2Y1 receptors in β-cells since functional ablation of the P2Y1 receptor attenuates the effect of IVM on insulin secretion in both wild-type and circadian mutant β-cells (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the genetic knockout data.

claim: Pharmacological enhancement of P2Y1 receptor activity may bypass pathological and circadian alterations in expression of the P2Y1 receptor in β-cells to restore insulin secretion.
source: Our analyses reveal that pharmacological enhancement of P2Y1 receptor activity may therefore bypass pathological and circadian alterations in expression of the P2Y1 receptor in β-cells to restore insulin secretion.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the data showing IVM rescues insulin secretion in circadian mutants.

claim: The P2Y1 receptor was implicated in nutrient- and ATP/ADP-dependent regulation of insulin release through an adipocyte-islet axis.
source: Recently, the P2Y1 receptor was implicated in nutrient- and ATP/ADP-dependent regulation of insulin release through an adipocyte-islet axis, further suggesting that P2RY1 may play a role in physiological regulation of islet hormone release (Prentice et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is based on recent literature, supported by citation.

claim: P2RY1 may play a role in physiological regulation of islet hormone release.
source: Recently, the P2Y1 receptor was implicated in nutrient- and ATP/ADP-dependent regulation of insulin release through an adipocyte-islet axis, further suggesting that P2RY1 may play a role in physiological regulation of islet hormone release (Prentice et al., 2021).
evidence: This is inferred from the cited work on P2Y1 in adipocyte-islet signaling.

claim: IVM may augment P2X-P2Y1 crosstalk to drive insulin secretion, which has been shown to drive Ca2+ and P2Y1-dependent activation of other cell types.
source: One possibility is that IVM may augment P2X-P2Y1 crosstalk to drive insulin secretion, which has been shown to drive Ca2+ and P2Y1-dependent activation of other cell types (Weng et al., 2008; Woehrle et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis based on prior literature, supported by citations.

claim: Previous physiological and transcriptomic studies have shown that circadian regulation of insulin exocytosis involves control of the expression and activity of cell-surface receptors and second messenger systems.
source: Previous physiological and transcriptomic studies have shown that circadian regulation of insulin exocytosis involves control of the expression and activity of cell-surface receptors and second messenger systems (Perelis et al., 2015; Gil-Lozano et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is based on prior work, supported by citations.

claim: The drug screen was based on the idea that modulators of insulin secretion in cells that lack a functional clock would complement prior genomic analyses revealing circadian control of peptidergic hormone exocytosis.
source: We based our drug screen on the idea that modulators of insulin secretion in cells that lack a functional clock would complement prior genomic analyses revealing circadian control of peptidergic hormone exocytosis and also to provide proof of principle that the clock can be leveraged to sensitize screening for new chemical modulators of β-cell function.
evidence: This is a statement of the rationale for the experimental approach.

claim: The clock can be leveraged to sensitize screening for new chemical modulators of β-cell function.
source: We based our drug screen on the idea that modulators of insulin secretion in cells that lack a functional clock would complement prior genomic analyses revealing circadian control of peptidergic hormone exocytosis and also to provide proof of principle that the clock can be leveraged to sensitize screening for new chemical modulators of β-cell function.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the methodological approach based on the successful screen.

claim: This approach identified Ca2+-dependent pathways as a potential route to ameliorate circadian disruption and enhance GSIS.
source: This approach identified Ca2+-dependent pathways as a potential route to ameliorate circadian disruption and enhance GSIS.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the identification of compounds that enhance calcium signaling.

claim: Previous small-molecule screens have identified glucose-dependent insulinotropic compounds in wild-type cells.
source: Previous small-molecule screens have identified glucose-dependent insulinotropic compounds in wild-type cells (Burns et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is based on prior literature, supported by citation.

claim: Several compounds identified in previous screens, including the anti-inflammatory bufexamac and anti-giardiasis drug lobendazole, were found to be ineffective or even inhibitory in the circadian mutant screen.
source: However, several of these compounds, including the anti-inflammatory bufexamac and anti-giardiasis drug lobendazole, were found to be ineffective or even inhibitory in our circadian mutant screen (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by the screening data showing these compounds did not enhance insulin secretion in circadian mutant cells.

claim: High-throughput screens may lead to more personalized therapeutics through comparison of insulinotropic compounds identified using cells without known mutations versus those discovered in cells harboring monogenic or polygenic diabetes variants.
source: In the future, high-throughput screens may lead to more personalized therapeutics through comparison of insulinotropic compounds identified using cells without known mutations versus those discovered in cells harboring monogenic or polygenic diabetes variants.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about future applications of the screening approach.

claim: Several of the compounds identified in the screen have been used in disease treatment and have known mechanisms of action, including the cholinergic activators carbachol and tacrine.
source: Several of the compounds identified in our screen have been used in disease treatment and have known mechanisms of action, including the cholinergic activators carbachol and tacrine (Linn et al., 1989; Crismon, 1994).
evidence: This claim is based on known uses of these compounds, supported by citations.

claim: The identification of cholinergic activators in the screen raises the intriguing possibility of using drug derivatives related to these molecules for type 2 diabetes treatment, particularly in the context of circadian/sleep disruption.
source: The identification of these compounds in our screen raises the intriguing possibility of using drug derivatives related to these molecules for type 2 diabetes treatment, particularly in the context of circadian/sleep disruption.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential therapeutic applications.

claim: The study of transcriptional rhythms across the 24 hr circadian cycle has previously revealed a diverse landscape of clock-controlled genes and pathways.
source: The study of transcriptional rhythms across the 24 hr circadian cycle has previously revealed a diverse landscape of clock-controlled genes and pathways (Zhang et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is based on prior literature, supported by citation.

claim: Limited advances have been made in utilizing information about clock-controlled genes to treat diseases associated with circadian disruption, including type 2 diabetes.
source: Despite the identification of thousands of tissue-specific and clock-controlled transcripts, limited advances have been made in utilizing this information to treat diseases associated with circadian disruption, including type 2 diabetes.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the field.

claim: One approach to treating circadian disruption has been to intervene and restore the molecular clock program using pharmacology (Nobiletin).
source: One approach to this challenge has been to intervene and restore the molecular clock program using pharmacology (Nobiletin) (He et al., 2016), micronutrient supplementation (NAD+ precursors) (Levine et al., 2020; Sato et al., 2017), or enforced behavioral rhythms (such as time-restricted feeding) (Sutton et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is based on prior literature, supported by citation.

claim: One approach to treating circadian disruption has been micronutrient supplementation (NAD+ precursors).

evidence: This claim is based on prior literature, supported by citations.

claim: The circadian timing system regulates the function of mature β-cells.
source: Since the circadian timing system has been shown to not only regulate the function of mature β-cells, but also the regenerative capacity of islets in both the context of the mouse (Petrenko et al., 2020b) and in human embryonic stem cell differentiation (Alvarez-Dominguez et al., 2020), molecules identified in cell-based genetic screens may provide broad applicability as therapeutics.
evidence: This claim is based on prior literature, supported by citations.
